messages:
sarah: Quick summary — I ran a region-by-region cost + perf pass for Q3 inference capacity. Early headline: SFO raw GPU price is slightly lower, but inter-region egress + PrivateLink peering to our EU customers makes LON cheaper for steady reserved capacity. TL;DR: placement matters a lot once egress and interconnect are counted.

arjun: Can you drop the numbers? interested in A100/H100 delta and how reserved commits change the breakdown.

sarah: Yep. Short table (per-month approx, $k):
```
Region  | GPU SKU | Spot/unit | Reserved/unit (1yr) | Avg egress per-request | Net per-token 
SFO     | H100    | 12.4      | 9.1                 | 0.6c                  | higher due to egress
LON     | H100    | 13.1      | 9.5                 | 0.14c                 | lower for EU traffic
SFO     | A100    | 8.7       | 6.4                 | 0.6c                  | cheaper small workloads
LON     | A100    | 9.2       | 6.8                 | 0.14c                 | best for reserved EU embed workloads
```
Numbers include committed use discount assumptions and estimated egress via cloud peering.

lucy: Where are we counting cross-region KV cache sync? that traffic spikes and sometimes shows up as 10-15% of egress.

sarah: We modeled cache sync as internal control-plane egress for multi-region replicas — added ~0.05c/request in the H100 case. If you colocate the cache (single-region primary) it drops but increases failover RTO.

darwin: (not in thread) might be helpful to see perf P95 delta too — higher RTT for LON -> slightly higher tokens/s for chat.
dmitri: @sarah can you paste the bill breakdown for last month for the SFO pool? curious if networking surges are consistent or spiky.
sarah: Pasted a small snippet from billing-bot: 
```
billing-bot: SFO-pool-2026-02: 
- Compute: $420k
- Networking (egress+interconnect): $78k
- Disk & infra: $34k
Total: $532k
LON-pool-2026-02:
- Compute: $460k
- Networking: $12k
- Disk & infra: $38k
Total: $510k
```
Note: SFO appears cheaper compute but networking swings it.

finance-ops: From finance side — if we commit 1yr reserved H100 in LON we can negotiate a 18% extra discount with the cloud rep (volume + commit). For SFO we can get burst credits but lower committed discount.

arjun: Interesting. For latency-sensitive chat endpoints, we should keep some triangular routing: front RNG in SFO for NA customers, but have model-serving pinned in LON for EU customers and for heavy batched workloads. Thoughts on split percentage?

dmitri: Given commit economics + peering, proposal: reserved capacity 60% LON (steady), 30% SFO reserved for baseline NA, 10% burst on preemptible/spot in nearest region. That reduces cross-region egress for EU by ~70%.

lucy: Ops note: LON has slightly lower NIC throughput quotas on the cheaper SKUs; if we pack more models per host we may see queuing at 99th percentile. Need to validate with a synthetic runner before moving all reserved there.
sarah: Agreed — plan: run 7-day soak with production load replay, A/B H100 vs A100 profiles, and measure 99p latency + network egress. If results match the cost model we proceed with commit negotiation.

finance-ops: If the soak shows parity, I'll open a purchase request for 1yr LON reserved H100 at the negotiated rate.

billing-bot: Note: remember to include interconnect commit line item in contract; otherwise egress rebate won't apply.

arjun: Action items:
- sarah: run soak and paste perf traces (due in 7 days)
- lucy: create runbook for NIC/QoS checks and limits in LON (3 days)
- dmitri: draft rollout plan & fallback to SFO if soak fails (5 days)
- finance-ops: standby to finalize PO if soak good (7 days)

sarah: Cool. If nobody objects, I'll kick off soak today and add a small proxy to route 70% EU traffic to LON during test. :white_check_mark:

arjun: :thumbsup: sounds good. Also @sarah can you add a couple of sample requests that amplify cache sync so we test worst-case egress?

sarah: On it.
